name: Sika Primer-3 N
paste:
SIKA® PRIMER-3 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Primer-3 N, July 2025, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sika_primer-3_n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Primer-3 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Primer-3 N is a solvent-based, 1-component primer.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sika® Primer-3 N is designed for use with Sikaflex®, SikaHyflex®, SikaBond®, SikaSeal® and Sikasil® products on porous substrates and metals.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Primer-3 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: SOLVENT BASED ONE COMPONENT PRIMER FOR POROUS SUBSTRATES AND METAL
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018 - Potable drinking water approved
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - ISO 3219: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Viscosity (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy to apply
    - Water repellent
    - Short flash-off time
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: 1-component, solvent-based epoxy resin compound
    - Colour: Transparent
    - Density: ~1.00 kg/l (ISO 2811-1)
    - Viscosity: ~10 mPas (ISO 3219)
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 250 ml bottle, 6 bottles per box; 1 l bottle, 4 bottles per box
    - Shelf life: 9 months from the date of production
2.7 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +25°C. Always refer to packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and homogeneous, free from oils, grease, dust and loose or friable particles. Cement laitance must be removed.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded coatings which could affect adhesion of the primer and sealant. The substrate should be of sufficient strength to withstand with the stress induced by the sealant during movement.
    - Use techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, grit blasting or other suitable mechanical methods to remove all weak substrate material. Repair all damaged joint edges with suitable Sika® repair products. Remove all dust, loose and friable material from all surfaces before application activators, primers or sealant. Where joints in the substrate are saw cut, after saw cutting, all slurry material must be flushed away and joint surfaces allowed to dry.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Consumption.
    | Yield per litre | Linear meters per litre |
    | On porous substrates | 5 m² | 250 m |
    | On non-porous sub- | 8 m² | 400 m |
    | strates |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.3 Flash-off time.
    | Maximum | 8 hours |
    | Minimum | 30 minutes |
4.4 Application method / tools. Apply Sika® Primer-3 N with a clean brush or roller to the substrate. Sika® Primer-3 N shall be applied only once. Tightly reseal the container immediately after each use.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use. Once cured, residual material can only be removed mechanically.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sika® Primer-3 N must be used within one month after opening the container.
    - Discard any primer that has gelled or separated.
    - Primers are adhesion promoters and are not a substitute for the correct preparation of a substrate, nor do they improve the strength of the surface significantly.
    - Avoid excessive application of primer causing puddles at the base of the joint.
4.7 Further documentation.
    - Safety Data Sheet
    - Pre-treatment Chart Sealing and Bonding
    - Method Statement Joint Sealing
    - Technical Manual Facade Sealing

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +5°C |
    | Minimum | +40°C |
5.3 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +5°C |
    | Minimum | +40°C |
    Note: The substrate temperature must be +3°C above dew point temperature and free from frost and ice.
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.00 kg/l (ISO 2811-1)
    - Viscosity: ~10 mPas (ISO 3219)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Primer-3 N, July 2025, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sika_primer-3_n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sika Primer 3 N, version 18/08/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/MSDS%20Sika%20Primer%203%20N%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® Primer-3 N, version 09/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/sds-sika-primer-3n.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
